page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro System and 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance runs on an AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core). It is configured with 256.0 GB of memory, representing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES encryption.

The m8gn.16xlarge incorporates a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating heavy ingress and egress demands. It contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for persistent or scratch volumes. The instance also excludes discrete hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystems. The platform achieved top-tier rankings in Geekbench multi-core performance (25,687.0), Clang compilation (81,021.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (674.62 GB/sec). Memory throughput showed top-tier figures across tests, including 480.5 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 235.58 GB/sec for large-block writes, translating into top-tier results for Redis SET operations at 140.57 million ops/sec and static web serving throughput at 115.57 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1899.0) and stress-ng single-core (1706.49), placed in the average tier.

Qualitatively, the Neoverse-V2 architecture offers strong compute density and memory bandwidth efficiency for highly parallelized software, though workloads bounded strictly by single-thread frequency or local disk I/O may encounter limitations. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, distributed caching layers, high-throughput static web serving, network-intensive microservices, and in-memory database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz and 256.0 GB of system memory. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with an arm64 architecture, it delivers 200 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance includes no discrete GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network storage for data persistence. Across benchmarks, the m8gn.16xlarge excels in parallelized execution, securing top-tier results in multi-core Geekbench tests, Clang compilation, uncached memory bandwidth, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations. Single-thread performance sits in the middle tier. Given its high network capacity, high memory bandwidth, and 64 dedicated cores, it is well suited for distributed in-memory databases, large-scale CI/CD build farms, parallelized ETL, and network-bound web serving workloads.
